title: AI in recruiting boosts accessibility, says Ribbon CEO
excerpt: Ribbon said its voice-based AI recruiting platform tools have improved accessibility by allowing candidates to interview at flexible times.
content_html:
AI is changing job interviews by letting candidates interview around the clock

By Katherine Li

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Job interviews are increasingly happening after most people have gone to bed.

Ribbon AI, a voice-AI recruiting platform, told Business Insider that about a quarter of interviews conducted through Ribbon take place between 10 p.m. and 2 a.m. local time, according to data from more than 500 companies using the service. Among Ribbon's manufacturing customers, that share rises to 35%.

Arsham Ghahramani, the CEO of Ribbon, told Alex Hutchings last week on the ThinkData podcast that the pattern may be driven by working parents with little spare time, or by workers in factories or kitchens who struggle to find a quiet place to be interviewed during the day.

"What initially seems like a technology where you're sort of removing the human out of the aspect, seems like maybe there will be like a disadvantage for the candidate, actually kind of flips the other way," Ghahramani said.

"Now you have candidates who could never have been interviewed before," Ghahramani added. "That's a huge accessibility piece."

Ribbon said the AI interview tool also improves 180-day employee retention by 10% to 30% across top customers, and a major auto manufacturer has been hiring 35% faster since adopting the tool.

'We are just not going back'

The use of AI in recruiting is gaining ground as employers look for ways to process a growing flood of applications. Two HR experts told Business Insider they're optimistic about how AI could reshape the interview process.

Tim Sackett, a veteran recruiter and CEO of HRUTech.com, told Business Insider that AI Interviewing might be "the best thing to ever happen" to inclusive hiring.

"For the first time in history, 100% of applicants are being able to interview and show their worth to the job," Sackett said. "I would estimate that we'll begin to see more inclusion within roles and companies as well, as more and more people get their 'at-bats' in the hiring process."

Steve Boese, Co-Chair of the HR Technology Conference, told Business Insider that technology-driven flexibility is a "net positive" for candidates.

"If hiring companies can offer 24/7 availability for these kinds of AI-brokered interviews, then they have removed a potential barrier for at least some candidates who by need or by choice will elect to take the interview at 1 a.m. or 2 a.m.," Boese said.

A Greenhouse survey released in May found that nearly two-thirds of applicants had been interviewed by an AI agent, up 13% points in six months. 38% of US candidates, however, responded to Greenhouse that they had abandoned a hiring process rather than interview with AI, while another 12% said they would do so if an AI interview were mandatory.

In the same Greenhouse survey, 36% of respondents said they felt evaluated differently because of age in both AI-led and human interviews, while 27% said the same due to race or ethnicity.

Research has found that large language models can absorb and reproduce stereotypes embedded in the data they are trained on. A 2025 Stanford study examining how generative AI depicts workers across industries, for example, found that ChatGPT's responses showed clear biases against older women and younger workers.

"While many people long for the 'old days' of live phone screens, in-person interviews, personal feedback, etc, we are just not going back to those processes at any scale," Boese added. "Tech has taken over most of the recruiting process, and AI is now replacing the legacy solutions."

content_html_zh:
人工智能正在改变求职面试，让候选人全天候面试

作者：Katherine Li 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

工作面试越来越多地发生在大多数人上床睡觉后。

语音人工智能招聘平台 Ribbon AI 告诉《商业内幕》，通过 Ribbon 进行的面试大约有四分之一发生在晚上 10 点到晚上 10 点之间。 和凌晨 2 点 当地时间，根据超过 500 家使用该服务的公司的数据显示。 在 Ribbon 的制造客户中，这一比例上升至 35%。

Ribbon 首席执行官 Arsham Ghahramani 上周在 ThinkData 播客上告诉 Alex Hutchings，这种模式可能是由几乎没有空闲时间的在职父母推动的，或者是由工厂或厨房的工人在白天努力找到一个安静的地方接受采访而造成的。

加赫拉马尼说：“最初看起来像是一种将人类排除在外的技术，看起来可能会给候选人带来不利，但实际上却恰恰相反。”

加赫拉马尼补充道：“现在的候选人以前从未接受过面试。” “这是一个巨大的可访问性部分。”

Ribbon 表示，AI 面试工具还将顶级客户的 180 天员工保留率提高了 10% 至 30%，自采用该工具以来，一家大型汽车制造商的招聘速度提高了 35%。

“我们只是不会回去”

随着雇主寻找处理越来越多的申请的方法，人工智能在招聘中的应用正在普及。 两位人力资源专家告诉《商业内幕》，他们对人工智能如何重塑面试流程持乐观态度。

资深招聘人员兼 HRUTech.com 首席执行官蒂姆·萨克特 (Tim Sackett) 告诉 Business Insider，对于包容性招聘来说​​，人工智能面试可能是“有史以来最好的事情”。

萨克特说：“历史上第一次，100% 的申请者能够参加面试并展示自己对这份工作的价值。” “我估计，随着越来越多的人在招聘过程中获得‘主动权’，我们将开始看到更多的角色和公司的包容性。”

人力资源技术会议联合主席史蒂夫·博斯 (Steve Boese) 告诉《商业内幕》，技术驱动的灵活性对候选人来说是“净积极因素”。

“如果招聘公司能够为此类人工智能中介面试提供 24/7 的可用性，那么他们至少为一些因需要或自愿选择在凌晨 1 点参加面试的候选人消除了潜在障碍。 或者凌晨 2 点，”博斯说。

Greenhouse 5 月份发布的一项调查发现，近三分之二的申请人接受过人工智能代理的面试，六个月内上升了 13%。 然而，38% 的美国候选人对 Greenhouse 表示，他们已经放弃了招聘流程，而不是接受人工智能面试，而另外 12% 的人表示，如果人工智能面试是强制性的，他们会这样做。

在同一项 Greenhouse 调查中，36% 的受访者表示，在人工智能主导的访谈和人类访谈中，他们因年龄而感到不同的评价，而 27% 的受访者则因种族或民族而表示相同的看法。

研究发现，大型语言模型可以吸收并再现嵌入其训练数据中的刻板印象。 例如，斯坦福大学 2025 年的一项研究调查了生成式人工智能如何描述各行业的工人，结果发现 ChatGPT 的反应显示出对老年女性和年轻工人的明显偏见。

“虽然许多人渴望回到现场电话屏幕、面对面采访、个人反馈等‘旧时代’，但我们不会再以任何规模回到这些流程，”博斯补充道。 “科技已经接管了大部分招聘流程，人工智能现在正在取代传统的解决方案。”
